title: My side Flux Team ⚡ — A whole team of local, open-source AI models working in parallel as colleagues for game dev (Unity/Godot integration coming!)
author: Key_Pin1034
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’m pretty nervous about posting this because I only started learning how to code about 1 or 2 months ago. I've been using AI tools to learn, push my limits, and see if I could build a complex system from scratch.

Instead of using one AI tool at a time, I built **Flux Team ⚡** — a framework where a whole team of open-source, local models work in parallel like real coworkers to help you build games.

**The Team Architecture:**

* 🧠 **Qwen3-8B** — The coordinator. It breaks down your game idea into specific development tasks.
* 🧱 **Hunyuan3D-2** — Generates 3D models directly from text or reference images.
* 🎵 **Audiocraft** — Handles dynamic music generation and SFX.
* 🏃 **FreeMoCap** — Creates animations from videos it autonomously searches and finds online.
* 🌊 **AInVFX Fluid** — Generates fluid and particle effects files.

**What's working right now:**

* **True Parallelism:** One chat interface (Grok-style UI) controls everything. The whole team works at the same time, not step-by-step.
* **Autonomous Web Browsing:** Each agent can browse the web on its own to research reference assets, documentation, and inspiration before starting to work.
* **One-Click Installer:** The installer automatically downloads, bundles, and sets up all \~21 GB of quantized models on the first run. No complex Python environments needed.
* **100% Local & Private:** Built with Electron + Python (FastAPI), using Ollama/llama.cpp for the LLM. Zero data is sent to third-party servers.
* **Totally Free:** No subscriptions, no paid APIs, no cloud costs. Everything runs entirely on your machine.

**Still building:**

* **The Live Bridge (Godot/Unity):** The ultimate goal is to open your editor and watch changes appear live in your scene. The backend and plugins are written, but they are not fully tested yet, which is why I don't have a demo video ready just yet.

Since I'm a beginner, my architecture might not be perfect or super clean, but I learned a ton making this. If the project gains enough traction and popularity, I will absolutely consider releasing it as full open-source on GitHub. No absolute promises for now — let's see how the community feels about it first.

I'm completely open to any questions about the project, the architecture, the multi-agent orchestration, or the models!.
